## WebSocket: complete QA guide

WebSocket is a persistent, full-duplex communication protocol for cases where both client and server need to send data at any time without creating a new HTTP request for every message. Typical uses are chats, live notifications, collaborative editing, multiplayer games, dashboards, trading/market feeds, device telemetry, presence indicators and other real-time features.

### WebSocket vs HTTP polling vs SSE

| Mechanism | Direction | Connection model | Good fit |
|---|---|---|---|
| HTTP request/response | Client → server, then response | Short-lived/logical request | CRUD, ordinary APIs, cacheable operations |
| Polling | Client repeatedly asks | Repeated HTTP requests | Simple low-frequency updates |
| Server-Sent Events (SSE) | Server → browser | Long-lived HTTP stream | One-way server events such as feeds/notifications |
| WebSocket | Both directions | Long-lived duplex connection | Interactive low-latency messaging |
